_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when discovering a domain through events, commands, actors, policies, aggregates, read models, external systems,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "map the order lifecycle as domain events before we design tables or APIs"
cases.context: The agent has access to the event-storming skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is event-storming the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes event-storming as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against system-interface-contracts, webhook-integration, api-design
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the event-storming workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore event-storming
Does not route to system-interface-contracts, webhook-integration, api-design when the event-storming scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
